intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that epidermolysis bullosa simplex-7 with nephropathy and deafness (EBS7) is caused by homozygous mutation in the CD151 gene on chromosome 11p15.5.

paragraphs.text: Epidermolysis bullosa simplex-7 with nephropathy and deafness (EBS7) is characterized by hereditary nephritis progressing to end-stage kidney disease, sensorineural deafness, and pretibial epidermolysis bullosa. Affected individuals lack the MER2 blood group antigen, which is carried by the tetraspanin CD151 (Kagan et al., 1988; Karamatic Crew et al., 2004).

paragraphs.text: Karamatic Crew et al. (2004) showed that CD151, a tetraspanin that forms stable laminin-binding complexes with integrins in kidney and skin and is encoded by a gene at the same position on chromosome 11p15.5 as the MER2 blood group gene, expresses the MER2 blood group antigen and is located on erythrocytes. In 3 MER2-negative patients of Indian Jewish origin with end-stage kidney disease, 2 of whom were sibs, they identified homozygosity for a 1-bp insertion (G383) in exon 5 of the CD151 gene, causing a frameshift and a premature stop signal at codon 140. The resulting truncated protein would lack its integrin-binding domain. The authors concluded that CD151 is essential for the proper assembly of the glomerular and tubular basement membrane in kidney, has functional significance in the skin, is probably a component of the inner ear, and could play a role in erythropoiesis.

agent.process_note: I read all 3 files in full. Kagan et al. (1988) has only a title, Karamatic Crew et al. (2004) has only an abstract, and Has et al. (2020) has only an abstract. The causal gene (CD151), zygosity (homozygous), variant (1-bp insertion G383 in exon 5, frameshift, stop at codon 140) and location (11p15.5) all come from the Karamatic Crew abstract. No CD151 MIM number was supplied, so I left it out. The abstracts do not say whether the Karamatic Crew sibs are the family Kagan described, so I did not link them. The Has et al. (2020) abstract does not mention CD151 or this subtype, so I did not cite it. Ages, consanguinity, functional studies and HGVS-standard variant names were not available.
